entry_points.text: Top level bring up runs with interrupts off through processor, memory, scheduler and timing setup, enables interrupts once, then finishes caching, namespace and accounting setup before delegating to the later init continuation.
Guarded invocation skips blacklisted targets, traces start, calls target, traces finish, validates execution state, then returns target result and mixes extra entropy.

Basic setup combines SMP cpuset finalization with driver model, interrupt proc setup, constructor execution and leveled calls; a separate pre SMP helper runs only the early table range with level tracing labeled early.
Post boot thread syncs async boot work, releases and hardens init memory while moving state toward running, then tries userspace candidates in strict priority and halts if none succeeds.

Early userspace setup creates device directory mode 0755, console node major 5 minor 1 with owner read write mode, and restricted root directory mode 0700; console attach opens the node and duplicates it onto descriptors 0 to 2, warning on open failure.

exports.text: Top level boot routine is globally visible for early platform handoff and never returns to its caller.
Single init routine invoker is exported so modular code can reuse the guarded invocation path.
Initial UTS namespace and version banner strings are globally visible for early identity and logging.

hazards.text: If ramdisk start lies below the lowest usable page frame, boot disables the ramdisk and emits a diagnostic to avoid overwritten early memory.
After each init routine the invoker checks preemption depth and interrupt state against entry values, warns on mismatch, restores entry depth and re enables interrupts left disabled.

invariants.text: Interrupts stay disabled from boot entry through early setup with a flag recording that state; early enable warns and is forced off, and one enable ends the window.
Blacklist takes comma separated names, copies each to owned storage on a global list, and matches by stripping module suffix at first space before exact compare, with diagnostics on list and veto.
Without symbol name support blacklisting is inert: listing warns and does nothing, veto check always allows.

Initcall debug timestamps start with caller identity, logs return and elapsed microseconds at finish, and logs each level name; one build uses tracepoints registered at enable, the other logs directly when the flag is set.
Global constructor iteration is skipped on UML where the host already ran them, though module constructor support stays enabled.

Userspace launch order is ramdisk command, then explicit command with halt on failure, then configured default with warn on failure, then sbin init, etc init, bin init, bin shell tolerating absence but warning when present yet not executable; all failing halts.

Freeable boot preparation enables fuller allocation and secondary CPUs, runs remaining early and leveled setup with health checks and built in tests, validates early userspace and root readiness including ramdisk command and conditional namespace work, then loads integrity material.

Read only hardening defaults on; arch hook consumes its option first, otherwise on and off toggle the flag and other values warn; strict mappings and checks apply only when build option and flag agree.
Early hostname copies its argument into the node name field with bounded length and warns on truncation.
Weak placeholders for initial namespace and boot banner let a stronger build provided object take precedence.

Boot, initcall, blacklist, trace and early userspace paths rely on ambient services from other dossiers for logging, diagnostics, IRQ control, string and symbol helpers and platform setup; those internals are not described here.

state_machines.text: Bring up orders scheduling usable before timers, timekeeping before full randomness, early workqueue admission before execution, and console after late slab readiness, ending in non returning handoff.

Leveled init walks eight named stages in fixed pure, core, postcore, arch, subsys, fs, device, late order over table slices bounded by per level markers, reparsing boot args per stage ignoring unknowns, plus a distinct early range before the first stage.

structs.text: Blacklist node pairs intrusive list linkage for global veto membership with a pointer to an owned zero terminated name copy.
Initial UTS namespace combines common namespace linkage with system, node, release, version, machine and domain name fields, anchored to the initial user namespace.
Level boundaries use nine ordered markers delimiting eight stages plus table end, paired with eight ordered stage names.
Two version banners exist: boot log banner identifying release builder host compiler and version, and proc format with release and version placeholders plus builder host and compiler.
